Conference USA · Tuesday, October 13, 2026 · 7:00 PM ET · Johnny “Red” Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro, TN (outdoor)

FinalMTSU 33, Delaware 30 — WINThe home dog won outright · graded +0.68u

OpenedMTSU +2.5Monday buyback point, via Action Network
We betMTSU +1.5FanDuel −110 · 1:52 PM ET card
Game day at DK+1.5 all dayNever moved in the hourly odds captures

The Story

Two 2-3 Conference USA teams on a Tuesday night, and we took the home dog for two independent reasons: Middle Tennessee’s 2-0 home start with the preview consensus lined up behind them, and a Delaware quarterback room in chaos — three passers used the week before and no starter named when the card locked at 1:52 PM. The news landed about an hour before kickoff: starter Nick Minicucci was out, and freshman Tyler Bell started instead. MTSU then won a 33-30 shootout outright — the +1.5 was never even needed.

The Evidence — everything we held, and whether it counted

Why we bet it

Home-dog spot & outside consensusConsidered · Led

MTSU is 2-0 at home; Delaware was laying points on the road. WagerTalk, Action Network staff and the iHeart model all took MTSU +1.5 — and RoadToCFB’s logged capper pick matches ours exactly (line_flag: clean).

Why it counted: lead angle #1 — the locked record’s home_field and sharp_consensus tags.

Delaware’s QB — unresolved at lock, OUT by kickoffConsidered · Led

At card time the starter was unresolved (intel claim #14): Action staff reported Nick Minicucci out for the season, WagerTalk / USA Today listed him questionable (knee), and Delaware had cycled three QBs in its loss to Liberty. The 6:36 PM pregame check still found no starter named. In the pregame injury report about an hour before kickoff he was ruled OUT, and freshman Tyler Bell took the first-team snaps (Delaware Online).

Why it counted: lead angle #2 — a flagged pending-resolution bet: part of this Conf 3 stake rode on news that landed after the card locked.

MTSU’s own quarterbackConsidered · Supported

Roman Gagliano: 8 TD against 1 INT, and MTSU listed no major injuries. Delaware was also without RB Greg Spiller (season) and WR Brandon Rehmann (questionable).

Why it counted: the healthy side of the QB contrast, from the pick’s written reasoning.

Models & model blendConsidered · Supported

Model blend spread +2.2 vs market +1.5 — no dissent. Model v0.2: spread +1.5, total 47.5 (exactly the market total).

Why it counted: agreement noted in the locked record; nothing in the models argued against the pick.

Market & line movementConsidered · Supported

Opened +2.5 at Monday’s buyback point (via Action Network). DraftKings held MTSU +1.5 in every hourly odds capture all day, and its MTSU moneyline sat at −105 until a late in-game print of +100; the total drifted 47.5 → 48.5, which wasn’t our market. Matrix sharp_side: with us.

Why it counted: the number we bet never deteriorated; movement was tracked via Action Network / WagerTalk reports.

Price & staking math

Breakeven 52.4% at −110; our estimated win chance 56% (+3.6 points of edge). Confidence 3 set the stake at 0.75 units; quarter-Kelly did not shrink it.

What we weighed against it

Counter-indicator — the injury tag’s recordConsidered · Opposed

Our injury_edge tag is 2-9 on the season. The red-team pass recorded it — and the pick was built to survive it: it does not lead with the injury alone, because the home-dog and consensus angles are independent of it.

Why it counted: documented in the locked record’s counter-indicator check; turnover-luck and vs_sharp flags: none.

What we had but didn’t use

Team efficiency splitsNot considered

Matrix: Delaware better on success rate (diff −0.098); MTSU better on defensive success allowed (+0.106) and pass-down explosiveness (+0.350).

Why not: captured in the feature matrix, but neither the locked record nor the written reasoning cites them.

Entering records & travel contextNot considered

Both 2-3 overall, both 3-2-0 ATS, both 1-4-0 on totals, both on two-game skids. Delaware traveled 638 miles across one time zone; rest 10 days vs MTSU’s 9.

Why not: substrate only — captured, with no documented role in the decision.

WeatherNot considered

Checked at card time (Weather.com hourly, Murfreesboro): ~85°F at kickoff, clear, wind SSW 6 mph, rain 1%.

Why not: below every threshold — no weather edge claimed.

Public betting splitsNot considered

No splits recorded for this game in either splits file; the picks card says “Splits via not recorded.”

Why not: not captured for this game.

Post-Game Verdict — did the evidence prove right?

Act 2 appended at grading. Final: MTSU 33, Delaware 30 — WIN, graded +0.68u.

Home-dog spot & consensus
MTSU won outright, 33-30. The +1.5 was insurance we never cashed.
Right
The QB resolution
Minicucci was out and a freshman started — the post-lock news broke our way. Honest footnote: Bell still drove Delaware to 30 points, so the win came from MTSU’s offense in a shootout, not a Delaware collapse.
Right
Models & model blend
The model blend leaned MTSU (+2.2); MTSU won by 3.
Right
Market & line
The +1.5 never moved at DraftKings and we won outright — no line value was gained or lost either way.
Didn’t matter
Injury-tag caution
The discounted angle wasn’t load-bearing, and it didn’t need to be.
Didn’t matter

Conference USA · Tuesday, October 13, 2026 · 8:00 PM ET · AmFirst Stadium, Jacksonville, AL (outdoor)

Live at buildFIU 30, Jax State 244th quarter, 9:37 left · our +3 loses only if Jax State wins by 4 or more

OpenedFIU +3Most books · only +2.5 at FanDuel / LetsBetMD
We betFIU +3BetRivers −112 · 1:52 PM ET card
Game day at DKJax State −3Pinned in every hourly odds capture

The Story

A low-total game (43.5) where the bet is the number as much as the team: a full field goal next to a defense allowing 12.2 points a game, in a game where points should be scarce. Our own model blend disagreed — it leaned Jacksonville State — and that documented dissent is exactly why this is a half-unit Confidence 2 instead of something bigger. Live at build time, FIU leads 30-24 late in the fourth quarter.

The Evidence — everything we held, and whether it counted

Why we bet it

The defense + the full field goalConsidered · Led

FIU allows 12.2 points per game — top-5 in total defense, and the only defense nationally to allow no more than four touchdowns through five games (intel claim #15). Last out: a 22-3 win allowing 230 yards. In a 43.5-total game, +3 covers a one-score loss — and the +3 was shopped: BetRivers, DraftKings and Fanatics held it while FanDuel hung only +2.5.

Why it counted: the lead angle — defense plus a key number, both named in the written reasoning.

Outside consensusConsidered · Supported

RG.org and the iHeart / Fox models also take FIU +3.

Why it counted: the locked record’s sharp_consensus and ats_trend tags — agreement, not origination.

Entering recordsConsidered · Supported

FIU 3-2 (3-2-0 ATS; totals 1-4-0), on a two-game win streak. Jacksonville State 4-2 (3-3-0 ATS), on a three-game win streak.

Why it counted: backs the ats_trend tag on the locked record; captured as-of in the feature matrix.

Price & staking math

Breakeven 52.8% at −112; our estimated win chance 55% (+2.2 points of edge). Confidence 2 sets the stake: 0.5 units.

What we weighed against it

Counter-indicator — our own models dissentedConsidered · Opposed

The model blend spread is −4.4 — it leans Jacksonville State, a −1.4 dissent against the pick. The v0.2 total model (50.5 vs a 43.5 market) also killed the FIU Under lean; that lean went to the watchlist instead.

Why it counted: the documented reason this shrank from a would-be Confidence 3 to Confidence 2 (tag: vs_model).

Counter-indicator — FIU’s road offenseConsidered · Opposed

FIU is 0-2 on the road this season with 19 points combined in those losses.

Why it counted: a real mechanism from the red-team pass — the offense has traveled badly, and this game is on the road.

Market money against usConsidered · Opposed

In numbers: open FIU +3 → our price +3 at BetRivers → DraftKings’ spread never left Jax State −3 all day, but its moneyline ran from −148 to −162 in the hourly odds captures. The 6:30 PM pregame check re-verified BetRivers still at +3 (−112) and logged the moneyline steam as a watch item, not a flip.

Why it counted: money moved toward the favorite while the key number held — noted, and the number is what we bought.

What we had but didn’t use

Team efficiency splitsNot considered

Success-rate diff dead even (+0.002); FIU edges in offensive success (+0.083) and explosiveness (+0.084).
